detail.longDescription: In high-risk OpSec architectures, a single unmutated frame is a permanent identity leak. The Packet Transformation Engine couples a Rust core with a C NFQUEUE adapter. But the real stealth happens at the egress. TC/eBPF hooks directly into the physical interface. It strictly validates raw ARP, EAPOL, and DHCP frames. If any downstream component leaks an unmarked or raw packet, the eBPF filter drops it instantly on the host's raw physical egress. Additionally, if the Packet Transformation Engine stops or crashes, bypass is strictly disabled. The system enforces a rigid fail-closed model. Τhe dedicated Guardian instantly kills the physical interface state (link down) while the firewall flushes all active connections. The network dies immediately to prevent any unmutated packet or signature leakage. Zero cleartext fallbacks, by design. # ph4ntxm # linux # debian # os # live # privacy # security # opsec # infosec # research # tech # technology
